conventions.convention: The domain is I × T³₂π, where I is a nonempty open real interval and the spatial coordinates are dimensionless angles. The positive scale factors a_i are C², time is measured in seconds, a_i in metres, and c in metres per second. The metric has signature (-,+,+,+), with time orientation N = ∂t.
H_i = ȧ_i/a_i, H = (H_1+H_2+H_3)/3, V = a_1a_2a_3, and σ² = (1/2)Σ_i(H_i-H)². The last quantity is the explicitly defined directional scalar, rather than an unspecified tensor-component norm.

R(X,Y)Z = ∇_X∇_YZ − ∇_Y∇_XZ − ∇_[X,Y]Z, with R(∂c,∂d)∂b = Rᵃ_bcd∂a and Ric_bd = Σ_a Rᵃ_bad. The C² coordinate construction is supplied locally on the translation-overlap quotient atlas; the published smooth definition is used for conventions, without silently extending its hypotheses.

The Kasner branch uses a_i = A_i(t/t_0)^{p_i} on a nonempty open interval contained in (0,∞), with A_i > 0, t_0 > 0 and real dimensionless p_i. The equivalence Ric = 0 iff Σp_i = Σp_i² = 1 excludes the all-zero exponent branch, which is treated separately.

The diagonal equations are explicit mathematical hypotheses, with continuous Q_i and constant Λ measured in m⁻². The unforced decay conclusion requires Q_1 = Q_2 = Q_3; otherwise the difference source remains.
The quotient and product constructions retain AC_ω only. The calculations make conditional geometric claims, without adopting a physical field law or reporting observations.

load_bearing.statement: For a diagonal Bianchi I datum, H_Σ = Σ_i H_i. The potentially nonzero lowered curvature components are the displayed sign-related families R_0i0i = −a_i²(Ḣ_i+H_i²) and R_ijij = a_i²a_j²H_iH_j/c². Ric_00 = −Σ_i(Ḣ_i+H_i²), Ric_ii = a_i²(Ḣ_i+H_iH_Σ)/c², and all off-diagonal Ricci components vanish.
On M = I × T³₂π, positive C² scale factors define g = −c²dt² + Σ_i a_i(t)²(dx^i)² and N = ∂t, together with H_i, H, V and σ² as explicitly displayed.

For the diagonal Bianchi I datum, the displayed Christoffel, curvature, Ricci, scalar and Einstein component formulas define the C² construction on local quotient charts. The connection coefficients are C¹, curvature is continuous, and the arrays agree on translation overlaps.
For the stated positive-time power-law branch with not all p_i zero, Ric = 0 holds exactly when P = Q = 1, where P = Σ_i p_i and Q = Σ_i p_i². If all p_i = 0, the full curvature tensor vanishes.

Under Gⁱ_i + Λ = Q_i(t), with no sum over i, Δ_ij = H_i − H_j satisfies Δ̇_ij + 3HΔ_ij = c²(Q_i − Q_j). If Q_1 = Q_2 = Q_3, each VΔ_ij is constant and σ² = CV⁻² throughout I for a constant C ≥ 0 with units m⁶s⁻².

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicitly inherited AC_ω assumption; the finite coordinate and exponent calculations use no additional choice.
The 2π-periodic three-torus quotient and periodic-coordinate conventions. No Sobolev estimate is invoked by this batch.
Pointwise signature and time-orientation definitions. The owned datum explicitly supplies its C² variant rather than asserting that its metric satisfies the supplier's smoothness hypothesis.
Curvature sign, component order and contractions. The required lower-regularity coordinate formulas and quotient patching are provided locally.
Constancy of VΔ_ij in the isotropic-source case. The consumer verifies continuity and differentiability on the nonempty open interval before applying it.
